deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a (presheaf) topos A with C = the class of monomorphisms as cofibrations, and W a class of 'weak equivalences' (a localizer). TF = C-injective maps (right lifting property against all monos, i.e. trivial fibrations). TC = trivial cofibrations. W~ is the class of weak equivalences of the model-type structure generated from some set ('bundle') of maps. The page notes that the natural generating family is not small, so one picks a small sub-bundle and asks what is needed to conclude W~ = W.

Inclusion W~ ⊂ W: this reduces to TC ⊂ W and TF ⊂ W.

(i) TF ⊂ W. Since TF is defined purely in terms of the monos, this inclusion could simply be imposed as an axiom on W. Better: take a separating interval I (two disjoint points 0,1 : e → I) that is injective (I → e in TF). The condition '(I → e) ∈ UW', i.e. I × X → X ∈ W for all X, makes every I-homotopy equivalence a weak equivalence. A trivial fibration f : X → Y is such an equivalence:
- a section s exists by lifting against ∅ → Y;
- a homotopy s∘f ~ id_X exists by lifting against the mono X × ∂I → X × I, where ∂I = e ⊔ e is a mono because I is separating.

The canonical choice is the Lawvere element L = Ω, the subobject classifier. It is injective and separating, and is labelled 'Lawvere element'. So the axiom becomes (1): L × X → X ∈ W for all X, and then every L-homotopism is in W. A crossed-out line had claimed equivalence with 'there exists a separating interval I with (I → e) ∈ UW'.

(ii) TC ⊂ W. First one needs (TC)_0 ⊂ W, the generating anodyne maps. For this the page states a needed property: W ∩ monos is stable under cobase change along monos. If i : S ↪ T is mono and g : S → S' is a mono in W, then the pushout f : T → S' ⊔_S T is in W.

The final diagram treats the generating maps A_0 × {e} ∪ B_0 × {e} → B_0 × I type inclusions. With A = A_0 × I ∪_{A_0×{e}} B_0 × {e}, the maps A_0 × {e} → A_0 × I and B_0 × {e} → B_0 × I are in W (homotopy equivalences). Two-out-of-three plus the pushout property then gives A ↪ B in W.

This is the skeleton of the construction of a cofibrantly generated model structure on a presheaf topos with monos as cofibrations, determined by a localizer W. It is precisely the programme later carried out by Cisinski (thesis 2002; Astérisque 308, 2006).
errors: The argument that TF maps are I-homotopisms only needs I separating (so that X×∂I ↪ X×I is mono). Injectivity of I is not needed for that step, though it matters elsewhere.
Going from 'all L-homotopisms in W' to W requires W to satisfy 2-out-of-3 (or saturation). This is used implicitly.

The crossed-out equivalence between the L-condition and 'some separating injective interval I with (I→e)∈UW' is not justified on the page. It is true up to the right hypotheses (Cisinski), which may be why Grothendieck struck it.

ideas.what: Monos as cofibrations on a topos, trivial fibrations = RLP wrt monos, and a reduction of W~=W to TF⊂W and TC⊂W
ideas.modern_name: Cisinski model structures on presheaf categories / localizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: D.-C. Cisinski (2002-2006), building on Grothendieck's Pursuing Stacks
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses modelizers and localizers; whether it contains this exact model-structure reduction is unsure

ideas.what: Using the subobject classifier Ω (the 'Lawvere element') as a canonical injective separating interval, with the axiom L×X→X∈W for all X
ideas.modern_name: Lawvere interval / Ω as canonical cylinder; the minimal localizer generated by L×X→X
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (Astérisque 308), who attributes the idea of the Lawvere interval to Grothendieck/Lawvere
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Pursuing Stacks (discussion of the 'Lawvere element' of a topos); unsure

ideas.what: Trivial fibrations are homotopy equivalences for a separating interval
Stability of W∩mono under pushout along monos, needed for anodyne maps
ideas.modern_name: Localizer axiom (cobase-change stability of trivial cofibrations); left-properness-type condition

missed.claim: In 1982-83 Grothendieck sketches, in essentially Cisinski's form, how a class W on a topos with monos as cofibrations yields a model structure. The ingredients are the Lawvere element axiom (L→e)∈UW, TF⊂W via L-homotopies, and pushout stability of mono∩W, together with an explicit smallness worry about the generating 'bundle'. This is a documented precursor of Cisinski's theory and of the Smith-type smallness argument.
missed.quote: Thus, the axiom is visibly (1) (L_A → e) ∈ UW  Lawvere element ... This implies that any L-homotopism is in W.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution: it shows how close Grothendieck came to the Cisinski model structures, including the smallness issue. The literature mostly credits Pursuing Stacks only for the notion of basic localizer and test categories.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear, explicit anticipation of Cisinski's model-structure theory on toposes using the Lawvere interval and the pushout axiom. However, this circle of ideas is broadly known to stem from Grothendieck's Pursuing Stacks period, and Cisinski acknowledges that lineage.
transcription_corrections: 'take [some] such bundle' is likely 'take such a bundle' / 'take some such bundle'.
The superscript annotation over L_A reads 'Lawvere element' (with an arrow pointing to L).
The rotated left-margin note is largely illegible. It appears to be a later comment, ending with '!!!', on not needing the assumption (or on a mistake). The transcription is uncertain.
'and' at the bottom is a catchword continuing to the next page; '15' is the archive page number; '6' at the top is Grothendieck's own page number.
